ping.summary: Send ICMP echo requests to see whether a host answers and how long replies take.
flags: stop after N requests (without it the simulator sends 4, then prints ^C)
seconds to wait for each reply
ping.note: No reply does not mean the host is down: firewalls often drop ICMP, so a ping sweep can undercount.

grep.summary: Show only the lines that match a pattern (from a pipe or a file).
flags: show lines that do not match

head.summary: Show the first lines of a file or a pipe.

tail.summary: Show the last lines of a file or a pipe.

cat.summary: Print files from your own machine (or pass a pipe through).

ls.summary: List the files on your own machine.

nmap.summary: Find which hosts are up and which ports accept connections.
flags: ports to scan: 22,80  or  1-1024  or  - for all (default: the common ports)
ping scan: list the hosts that are up, no port scan
ask each open service for its version
skip the up/down check and scan anyway
do not look up host names
show only open ports (and only hosts that have some)
nmap.note: Targets: a name, an address, a network (10.20.0.0/24) or a range (10.20.0.1-30). You are an ordinary user here, so scans use ordinary connections; options that need root (-sS, -sU, -O) are refused, as on a real machine. The up/down check connects to ports 80 and 443; as root on the local network nmap would use ARP instead.

ss.summary: List the sockets on this machine: listening ports and open connections.
flags: show port numbers, not service names
show the process (only for sockets you own)
ss.note: A socket bound to 127.0.0.1 can only be reached from this machine; one bound to 0.0.0.0 is reachable from the network.

netstat.summary: The older tool for the same job as ss.
netstat.note: Many systems now ship ss instead of netstat; the information is the same.

dig.summary: Ask a name server a question and see the whole answer: records, flags, which server replied.
flags: ask this server instead of the lab's resolver
reverse lookup: the name that owns an address (PTR)
record type (or put it after the name)
dig.note: The status line tells the story: NOERROR with an answer, NOERROR with none (the name exists but has no record of that type), NXDOMAIN (no such name), SERVFAIL (the server could not find out). The aa flag means the server owns the zone.

nslookup.summary: A quick name lookup: the server asked, then the answer (one question per command here).
flags: an address is looked up in reverse (PTR)
the address of the name server to ask
nslookup.note: A name without a dot gets the search domain added first (web-03 becomes web-03.corp.local). Interactive mode is not available in the simulator.

curl.summary: Fetch a web page, or just its headers, and see what the server announces about itself.
flags: send HEAD and show only the response headers
show the headers and then the page
silent: no error messages (-S shows them again)
give up connecting after s seconds
curl.note: Headers such as Server and X-Powered-By tell an attacker the software and its version. Plain http only: https, -L (follow redirects) and -v are not simulated.

ip.summary: Show this machine's network cards, addresses and routes (the modern ifconfig and route).
flags: IP addresses on each interface (a for short)
the cards themselves: state and MAC address
where traffic goes; the default route is the gateway
ip.note: The line starting default via is this machine's gateway. Commands that change anything (add, del, set) are refused in the simulator.

file.summary: Identify what kind of file something is by its header, not its name (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).

nm.summary: List a binary's symbol table (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).

strings.summary: Show the printable text embedded in a binary (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).
flags: only strings at least N characters long

readelf.summary: Show one part of an ELF binary's own description of itself (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).

objdump.summary: Disassemble one function of a binary (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).
flags: Intel syntax (the only one this simulator prints)

checksec.summary: A short report of a binary's exploit mitigations (binary exploitation skill only: no mission here uses it).
